facts.text: The applicant was born in 1984 and lives in Bursa.

anchor.surface_text: 2.  The applicant was born in 1984 and lives in Bursa. He was granted legal aid and was represented by Ms R. Doğan, a lawyer practising in İzmir.

facts.text: The applicant suffers from intellectual and physical disabilities.

anchor.surface_text: 5.  The applicant suffers from intellectual and physical disabilities.

facts.text: On 15 and 18 May 2002 the applicant was taken to a construction site by four children, one under 12, two under 13, and one just under 17 years old.

anchor.surface_text: 6.  On 15 and 18 May 2002 he was taken to a construction site by four children, one of whom was under 12 years old, two of whom were under 13 years old and the other who was just under 17 years old at the time.

facts.text: According to the applicant’s statement of 24 May 2002, on 15 May 2002 one child threatened him with a knife, two held him and pulled his trousers down, and the fourth raped him; they took turns raping him.

anchor.surface_text: According to the applicant’s statement, drawn up by a public prosecutor on 24 May 2002, on the first occasion one of the children had put a knife up against his throat and the other two had held him and pulled his trousers down while the remaining child had penetrated him with his penis.

facts.text: On 18 May 2002 the children tied a rope around the applicant's neck and raped him; they threatened to kill him if he told anyone.

anchor.surface_text: On the second occasion they had tied a rope around his neck and had penetrated him with their penises. They also told him that if he were to tell anyone what had happened, they would kill him.

facts.text: Criminal proceedings established that the applicant had been raped by three of those individuals.

anchor.surface_text: The criminal proceedings (see paragraph 11 below) established that the applicant had been raped by three of those individuals.

facts.text: Three of the applicant’s attackers were under 15 years old at the time of the attacks.

anchor.surface_text: In view of the fact that three of the applicant’s attackers had been under 15  years old at the time of the attacks, the public prosecutor in charge of the prosecution separated the criminal proceedings by instituting proceedings in respect of those three individuals before the İzmir Juvenile Court on 4 July 2002 and instituting ordinary proceedings before the Bergama Assize Criminal Court in respect of the fourth attacker on 27 May 2002.

facts.text: The public prosecutor separated the criminal proceedings: proceedings against three minors before İzmir Juvenile Court on 4 July 2002, and against the fourth attacker before Bergama Assize Court on 27 May 2002.

anchor.surface_text: In view of the fact that three of the applicant’s attackers had been under 15  years old at the time of the attacks, the public prosecutor in charge of the prosecution separated the criminal proceedings by instituting proceedings in respect of those three individuals before the İzmir Juvenile Court on 4 July 2002 and instituting ordinary proceedings before the Bergama Assize Criminal Court in respect of the fourth attacker on 27 May 2002.

facts.text: On 2 August 2002, the İzmir Juvenile Court joined both sets of proceedings and they continued before the Bergama Assize Court.

anchor.surface_text: On 2 August 2002, at the request of the Bergama Assize Court, both sets of proceedings were joined by a decision of the İzmir Juvenile Court, and they continued before the Bergama Assize Court.

facts.text: On 5 November 2003 the Bergama Assize Court declined jurisdiction and sent the case back to the İzmir Juvenile Court due to an amendment changing the age of juvenile court jurisdiction from 15 to 18.

anchor.surface_text: On 5 November 2003 the Bergama Assize Court issued a decision declining jurisdiction and sent the case back to the İzmir Juvenile Court, having regard to the amendment of 30 July 2003 to the Law on Juvenile Courts which had, inter alia, changed the age at which a child should be tried in the juvenile courts from 15 to 18.

facts.text: On 11 December 2004 one of the accused, just under 17 at the time of the attack, died; the İzmir Juvenile Court discontinued proceedings against him.

anchor.surface_text: On 11 December 2004 one of the accused, who had been just under 17 years old at the time of the attack, died. The İzmir Juvenile Court discontinued the proceedings in respect of him.

facts.text: On 26 September 2007 the İzmir Juvenile Court acquitted the other three accused due to lack of evidence, finding it impossible to determine if they had attained sexual maturity necessary for the offence.

anchor.surface_text: In respect of the other three accused, the court acquitted them on account of a lack of evidence, finding in particular that it was impossible to determine whether at the time of the attack they had had attained the sexual maturity necessary to be capable of committing the sexual offence in question. That decision was given on 26 September 2007.

facts.text: On 3 July 2012 the Court of Cassation upheld discontinuation of proceedings against the deceased accused, rectified acquittal of the youngest accused (under 12 at time of attack), and quashed acquittals of two others for rape and false imprisonment due to expiry of limitation for threats but not for rape.

anchor.surface_text: In its decision of 3 July 2012 on appeal, the Court of Cassation upheld the first-instance court’s decision to discontinue the proceedings in respect of the accused who had died. In respect of the youngest accused, it rectified the decision acquitting him on the basis that there had been no need to give a decision as he had not attained the age of criminal responsibility, having been less than 12 years old at the time of the attack. As regards the other two accused, the Court of Cassation noted that the limitation period for prosecution had expired in respect of the offence of making threats. However, it quashed the acquittal in respect of the offences of rape and false imprisonment, finding, on the basis of expert opinions and other evidence in the case file, that those acts had in fact taken place.

facts.text: Following remittal, the first-instance court discontinued false imprisonment charges due to expiry of limitation period and sentenced two accused to 3 years, 7 months, 22 days imprisonment for repeated rape under Article 102 § 2 of the current Criminal Code.

anchor.surface_text: Following remittal, the first-instance court discontinued the charges of false imprisonment on account of the expiry of the limitation period for prosecution of that offence. On the charges of repeated counts of rape, it sentenced the two accused to three years, seven months and twenty-two days’ imprisonment, under Article 102 § 2 of the current Criminal Code, in view of that Code having more lenient provisions than the former Criminal Code.

facts.text: On 29 January 2015 the Court of Cassation upheld discontinuation of false imprisonment charges and set aside rape convictions due to expiry of limitation period under current Criminal Code.

anchor.surface_text: Both the accused and the applicant appealed against the judgment of the first-instance court. On 29 January 2015 the Court of Cassation upheld the part of the judgment with respect to the discontinuation of the proceedings as regards the charges of false imprisonment. It also set aside the conviction for rape on the grounds that the time-limit for prosecution of that offence had also expired in the meantime in accordance with the provisions of the current Criminal Code, which specified a time-limit of eleven years and three months.

facts.text: On 30 April 2015 the applicant lodged an individual application with the Constitutional Court complaining that the criminal proceedings against his attackers had been ineffective.

anchor.surface_text: On 30 April 2015 the applicant lodged an individual application with the Constitutional Court, complaining that the criminal proceedings brought against his attackers had been ineffective.

facts.text: On 23 January 2019 the Constitutional Court held there was a violation of the State’s procedural obligations under Article 3 because the criminal proceedings had taken too long, resulting in discontinuation due to expiry of limitation period.

anchor.surface_text: In a decision of 23 January 2019 the Constitutional Court held that there had been a violation of the State’s procedural obligations under Article 3 of the Convention because the criminal proceedings, while not being complex, had taken too long, resulting in their discontinuation owing to the expiry of the limitation period.

facts.text: The Constitutional Court awarded the applicant 25,000 Turkish liras (approximately 4,145 euros) and reimbursement of legal costs, rejecting remainder of claims for non-pecuniary damage.

anchor.surface_text: With that finding, it awarded the applicant 25,000 Turkish liras (TRY) – approximately 4,145 euros (EUR) on the date of the decision – and the reimbursement of his legal costs, while rejecting the remainder (TRY 475,000 – approximately EUR 78,000) of his claims for non-pecuniary damage.

arguments.claim: The applicant argued that the compensation awarded by the Constitutional Court was insufficient given his suffering, the failure to anonymise his name, threats, humiliation, and worsening disability, and that the Constitutional Court had jurisdiction to award higher compensation.

anchor.surface_text: The applicant contested the Government’s submissions, arguing that the amount of compensation awarded by the Constitutional Court had been insufficient in view of his suffering, which had been further exacerbated during the criminal trial by the failure of the trial courts to anonymise his name and to conduct the hearings in camera. Moreover, on account of constant threats made by his attackers’ families and the humiliation suffered by his family, he and his family had had to move to another city. The attack and further anguish caused by the events surrounding the trial had resulted in the worsening of his disability. All these additional elements, which had been raised before the Constitutional Court, had been ignored by it. The applicant further submitted that the Constitutional Court had jurisdiction to award higher amounts of compensation. By way of example, the applicant referred to a case in which that court had awarded TRY 90,000 (approximately EUR 6,000 on the date of that court’s decision) to an applicant who had been subjected to treatment contrary to Article 3 by police officers.

arguments.court_reasoning: The Court considered the individual circumstances and found the compensation insufficient.
